messages:
Elena: FYI — spotted a negative adjustment on the Azure Marketplace invoice for ChannelEdge. Looks like a promo prorate applied twice for the Feb billing window. Attaching the relevant invoice lines below. :eyes:

Elena: ```
INVOICE_ID: INV-20260228-CH-9921
PARTNER: ChannelEdge
SKU: azure.marketplace.redwood.standard
USAGE_UNITS: 12,345
CHARGE: $1,234.56
ADJUSTMENT: -$246.91
ADJ_REASON_CODE: promo_prorate_v2
NOTE: promo_prorate_v2 appears twice in charge pipeline
```

Ravi: ouch. do we know which rollout touched ChannelEdge?

Maya: we did a targeted pricing experiment (promo_prorate_v2) for 10% of channel partners starting 2026-02-15. ChannelEdge was in the cohort. Looks like the billing pipeline applied both the legacy prorate and the new promo logic for trial-day customers. :facepalm:

Connor: tagging @Legal — are vendor clawbacks permitted under our marketplace agreements, or do we need partner consent before reversing an adjustment?

BillingBot: Adjustment queued: adj_id=ADJ-83472 status=processing (system)

Maya: quick assessment: the net impact to Redwood revenue is $246.91 for this partner period. Two options: 1) issue a one-off credit and reverse the vendor clawback to make partner whole, or 2) honor the clawback and absorb the negative adjustment (we'd then mark this experiment as causing billing regressions).

Elena: partner has already flagged this with their channel manager, asking for explanation. They expect a fix + credit.

Ravi: do we have precedent? last year we reversed a marketplace vendor claim for a telemetry double-count — got signoff from Alicia.

Alicia: I need the evidence chain (logs showing double-apply) + estimated impact across partners before I sign off. Can someone drop the minimal forensic notes here?

Maya: plan: 1) RevOps will extract billing pipeline logs for 2026-02-14..2026-03-01 and grep for promo_prorate_v2 events, 2) dev infra will capture the rollout toggle history, 3) Legal will confirm contract posture. ETA 24h. I'll paste the grep commands and sample output: 

Maya: ```
# search billing events for promo_prorate_v2
grep -R "promo_prorate_v2" /var/logs/billing/2026-02-* | sed -n '1,50p'
# sample hit
2026-02-20T03:11:02Z invoice_pipeline: invoice_id=INV-20260228-CH-9921 event=apply_promo promo=promo_prorate_v2
2026-02-20T03:11:02Z invoice_pipeline: invoice_id=INV-20260228-CH-9921 event=apply_prorate promo=legacy_prorate
```

Connor: Legal: based on our contract we can issue discretionary credits to partners; clawbacks initiated by marketplace vendors need evidence and partner notification. So best approach is to remediate and issue credit unless RevOps finds a clear partner-caused misreporting.

Ravi: sounds fine. can we also check how many partners are in the cohort — if this is widespread we need a mitigation rollback and a possible JV notice to Azure marketplace ops.

Maya: cohort query: roughly 47 partners. Early scan shows 4 partners with small negative adjustments (< $500). ChannelEdge is the largest among those. Will share a summary table in thread when done.

Elena: Action item: RevOps (Maya) to produce forensic snippet + summary across cohort. Finance (Alicia) to approve one-off credit if evidence confirms double-apply. Legal (Connor) to confirm notification language. I will reply to ChannelEdge with provisional timeline (24-48h) and that we're prioritizing reversing unintended adjustments. :pray:

Alicia: ok — pls drop the summary and I will review asap. Marking needs-approval.

BillingBot: adj_id=ADJ-83472 status=ready_for_review (system)

Elena: thanks all — I'll hold off on partner comms until Maya posts the log extract.

Ravi: bump in 12h if no updates. :clock12:
